html:
The Sissipahaw, or Haw, were a small Native American people of central North Carolina, living along the Haw River near today's Saxapahaw, which keeps their name. Little is known of them.

They may appear in the records of the Spanish expedition of Juan Pardo in the 1560s, and English traders mention them around 1700. After the Yamasee War of 1715 they disappear from the record; survivors probably joined the Catawba or other Piedmont peoples. Their neighbours included the Occaneechi.
